prompts.task: Read the loaded skill's shared ../references/splunk-agent-observability.md and ./service/eval/inputs/ao-root-compatibility-evidence.json. This is a bounded supplemental contract review, not the skill's usual whole-service workflow. The actual ./service/app.py is independent of these source fixtures. Review the supplied evidence only; do not browse, call cloud/models, start a service, install dependencies, run an application, or edit source/config/canonical reports. Write only ./service/.observe/ao-root-audit-review.md and .json. The JSON must identify evidence_basis, per_case decisions/mapping/proof_limits, and future_acceptance; the Markdown must explain the concrete choices. Keep captured synthetic diagnostics, source proposals, local tests, receiver receipt and current application/cloud proof separate. Assess source-owned AO root compatibility and propose canonical finding/acceptance content for each source case without creating or selecting new executable work. Distinguish the outermost agent from the physical transport root; explain each source role and which root/ancestor is absent or unproven in AO. Keep the existing-parentless captured observation scoped to that observation and preserve the unrelated service application. Explicitly review web-entrypoint-root-regression: its direct-agent unit test passes, its real Flask request has a generic HTTP parent, its bound audit has only resource/routing and agent-role work, and the captured cloud graph has five retained operation spans under a missing physical root. State the concrete role-specific handoff and result; do not treat selected routing work or the bare-function test as root proof. Also assess conversation-state-controller from its actual history, commit and rollback lifecycle. Distinguish it from transport-only-agent despite both calling one agent. Address its legacy serializer behavior and define actual HTTP success/failure plus unrelated health/reset acceptance. The new captured controller traces are isolated synthetic observations, not fresh execution of any source fixture or the original application.

judge_inputs: Inspect the supplied source cases and captured topology/results, the loaded shared AO-Compatible Trace Root contract, .observe/ao-root-audit-review.md/.json, last_message.md and grade.json. Judge concrete mapping decisions and evidence boundaries, not copied headings or policy wording.
rubric: Reconstructs the actual transport -> agent -> model/child graph and identifies the missing AO parent despite HTTP 200 with zero reported rejections. Correctly interprets all captured cases, including the failed marker-only and OpenInference cases and successful explicit workflow combination, without claiming any single field is sufficient or that the observed classifier behavior is universal.

Separates source roles: staged-controller owns a genuine two-stage orchestration; transport-only-agent is not relabeled as a workflow; existing-parentless-agent is preserved; nested agents stay connected to their real parent. Preserves native identities, correct kinds, one producer/provider and one export path, without dummy workflows, detached agents, duplicate roots or wholesale SDK migration.

Keeps implementation and evidence scope honest: proposals/source snapshots and synthetic diagnostics do not prove fresh application/cloud assembly. Unavailable cloud readback remains unproven; unsupported truthful root mappings have exact actionable compatibility blockers. Existing captured compatible evidence remains qualified rather than invented as a new run.

Defines acceptance that matches native/external identities, retained AO root and required operation/connecting-parent edges, rejects an absent parent or Partial trace placeholder after accepted export, and distinguishes source/local/receiver/cloud outcomes. Includes a real application error-path check without fake output and a nested-parent check.

Applies changes only to selected AO work. Leaves ao-excluded and unrelated service source, resources, profiles, destinations and canonical selections untouched. Preserves actual provider-error status/error.type and absence of model/controller output; available conversation identity comes from source, never a telemetry-only fallback.

Proposes source-backed root compatibility finding content and executable acceptance in the existing ledger without auto-selecting work, treating source-only root support as proved, or editing the application/canonical artifacts in this supplemental task.

For web-entrypoint-root-regression, identifies POST /chat SERVER as the physical root and invoke_agent as its child, exposes the omitted root finding/compatibility blocker separately from project/stream/routing, and does not silently expand selected scope. Requires the actual framework entrypoint for local root acceptance and marks the observed missing AO root as failed/incomplete despite successful forwarding. Does not blame localhost or cloud unavailability, relabel transport-only HTTP as a workflow, or claim that a passing parentless run_turn unit test proves the web graph. Gives concrete audit/selection follow-up and preserves the captured-versus-new-execution boundary.

For conversation-state-controller, recognizes a source-owned conversation workflow outside the single child agent, proposes or evaluates a supported same-span mapping while preserving SERVER kind and actual parent identities, and keeps health/reset routes ordinary HTTP. Does not mistake a single agent child for transport-only ownership or relabel the child agent. Authors a distinct actionable root finding/acceptance for the selected controller lifecycle and typed content rather than only an unsupported-mapping blocker; captured synthetic success/error cases do not close the source application gap.
